subject: Incident-led deployment options and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Burns <alex.burns@fininsights.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-19T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: production throttle and next steps

Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side: between 15:20-15:50 PST we hit a token-based throttling limit on the Hosted API which impacted our realtime assistant (5-8 TPS bursts; median latency spiked to ~420ms). We attached a short incident summary (logs redacted) for reference.

We need two things urgently:
- Immediate mitigation so we don't degrade UX tonight (can you bump capacity or suggest a routing/fallback?)
- Clear options and timelines to move from Hosted -> Dedicated or Private VPC. Procurement & Legal want an estimated lead time for Dedicated reserved capacity vs a VPC/on-prem deployment. Also confirm KMS options (we need keys retained in our GCP KMS).

We are aiming to decide by EOD tomorrow. Please send a concise mutual action plan with cost delta and cutover timeline. If Dedicated is the fastest path, what's the soonest we can be live (hours/days)? If VPC, what are realistic calendar estimates and prerequisites?

Regards,
Alex Burns
VP Product, FinInsights

Attachment: incident_report_20260719.pdf (pdf)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Burns <alex.burns@fininsights.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-19T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: production throttle and next steps

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the incident report. Short post-call recap and actionable next steps from our side: 

1) Immediate night-of mitigation (hours)
- We can temporarily raise your Hosted concurrency cap for the next 24 hours to absorb the burst while we validate patterns. This is a short-term safety valve; it does not guarantee long-term SLOs.
- Alternative: route heavy traffic to a lower-cost model variant we have pre-warmed for bursts (will slightly change token quality).

2) Short-medium term (1–5 business days) — Dedicated reserved capacity
- Fastest route to predictable throughput. We can provision a dedicated GPU pool and perform a quick routing cutover. Typical SLA-backed Dedicated onboarding: 2–5 business days depending on legal/PO.
- We'll need an expected RPS/RPM profile (burst and steady-state) and a target latency SLO to size the pool. A lightweight load test works great.

3) VPC / Private deployment (2–6+ weeks)
- Private VPC with customer-managed KMS and VPC peering takes more planning (networking, security, and possibly on-prem packaging). If you have strict KMS residency needs, this path meets them but has longer lead time.

Immediate asks from us to finalize a recommendation:
- Confirm target steady-state RPS and worst-case burst size (tokens/sec).
- Confirm legal/procurement timeline constraints (PO vs SOW vs immediate credit).
- Confirm whether Private KMS (GCP) is a hard requirement or preferred.

I'll loop in Dev (SE) and Marissa (AE) to provide a quick capacity estimate and a one-page mutual action plan for your procurement team. If you agree, I can also initiate a temporary cap increase tonight.

Proposed next step: 30-minute follow-up tomorrow 09:00 PST to review numbers and sign off. Calendly: https://calendly.com/jonas-weber/30

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Jonas / Marissa / Dev — thanks, that plan looks workable. We want to move forward with Dedicated reserved capacity as the fastest reliable path. Procurement will process a PO for an initial 3-month reserved pool with an option to expand. Please: 

- Send the one-page mutual action plan + SOW and the DocuSign proposal.
- Confirm you can stand up the Dedicated hot pool within 48 business hours of PO (we expect to have PO processed within 24 hours).
- Provide SOC2 summary and any attestations; Legal wants to confirm logs/retention options.

I’ve attached our incident report again and listed the key decision owners: Sarah Lin (Procurement) and Priya Natarajan (Security). We need pricing and the DocuSign by EOD today if possible.

Alex Burns
VP Product, FinInsights
